title: Who Has the Most Passing Yards in OU History? Landry Jones
question: Who is Oklahoma's career passing yards leader?
answer: Landry Jones is Oklahoma's career passing leader with 16,646 yards and 123 touchdown passes as the Sooners' quarterback from 2009 to 2012. That is more than 4,300 yards ahead of No. 2 Baker Mayfield (12,292) through the 2025 season.
summary: Landry Jones holds OU's career passing record with 16,646 yards and 123 TDs, more than 4,300 yards clear of Baker Mayfield. Here is the full top five.
body: Oklahoma has produced Heisman quarterbacks, No. 1 draft picks and national champions, but the career passing yards record belongs to a four-year starter: Landry Jones. Over the 2009 through 2012 seasons, Jones threw for 16,646 yards and 123 touchdowns, completing 1,388 of 2,183 attempts.

The margin is what makes the record so durable. Baker Mayfield is second with 12,292 yards, Sam Bradford third with 8,403, Jason White fourth with 7,922 and Josh Heupel fifth with 7,456. Jones's lead over Mayfield is more than 4,300 yards, which is more than a full season of production even for an elite passer.

Volume is the key. Jones attempted 2,183 passes for Oklahoma, while Mayfield needed only 1,157 attempts for his total. Mayfield was far more efficient per throw, but nobody in Sooners history has matched Jones's sheer workload.

Jones also dominates the single-game list. He owns five of the top ten passing games in school history, led by 554 yards at West Virginia in 2012, plus 505 at Kansas State in 2011 and 500 against Oklahoma State in 2012.

Since Mayfield, the best career total by a Sooners quarterback belongs to Dillon Gabriel, who threw for 6,828 yards in 2022 and 2023, well under half of Jones's mark, so the 16,646 record looks safe for a long time.
